definitions.explanation: A district or neighborhood where geisha houses, teahouses, and traditional entertainment establishments are concentrated. Historically the center of traditional Japanese performing arts and hospitality.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{花街|かがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
{花街|かがい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いている→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: Efforts to preserve the culture of the geisha districts continue.

examples.japanese: {祇園|ぎおん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{花街|かがい}で、⟦{舞妓|まいこ}→舞妓：15099_maiko⟧さん⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Gion is Japan's most famous geisha district, where you can see apprentice geisha.

notes:
FORMS:
{花|か} (flower) + {街|がい} (district, quarter). The 'flower' metaphor refers to the beauty and refinement of the arts practiced there.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kyoto's five major {花街|かがい} are {祇園甲部|ぎおんこうぶ}, {祇園東|ぎおんひがし}, {先斗町|ぽんとちょう}, {上七軒|かみしちけん}, and {宮川町|みやがわちょう}. Tokyo also had its own {花街|かがい}, such as {新橋|しんばし} and {赤坂|あかさか}. These districts are associated with traditional arts including ⟦{日本舞踊|にほんぶよう}→日本舞踊：28381_nihonbuyou⟧, ⟦{三味線|しゃみせん}→三味線：04464_shamisen⟧, and the tea ceremony.

ALTERNATE READING:
Also read as はなまち, which is more colloquial.

- {花街|かがい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{伝統|でんとう}→伝統：09585_dentou⟧ (traditions of the geisha districts)
